title: Alert creation wizard with SLO-sensitivity simulation and inline postmortem suggestions
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Design an end-to-end alert creation flow that surfaces SLO sensitivity 'what-if' simulation and suggests contextual incident artifacts (postmortems, runbooks, on-call handoff notes) inline. Goal is to reduce misconfigured alerts, speed on-call handoffs, and make alert config decisions visible to non-SRE stakeholders.
acceptance_criteria: User can create an alert using a step-by-step wizard that maps to existing alert fields (conditions, thresholds, receivers, routing).
Wizard includes a SLO-sensitivity panel which simulates how the candidate alert affects SLOs over chosen windows using historical data sampling.
Inline suggestions surface related postmortems/runbooks and allow quick-linking to selected artifacts during alert save.
Prototype validated with 3 PM/Eng sessions and Nielsen-style usability test (5 participants) with no major usability blockers.
Figma prototype handed off with tokens, component specs, and responsive states for desktop and tablet.
Handoff UX includes a compact timeline snippet that will be used by Eng to implement the on-call preview API call.
Design review sign-off from Product and Observability team recorded in comments.

risk_and_tradeoffs: SLO simulation requires sampled historical data; for short retention customers results may be noisy. To mitigate, show confidence ranges and require an explicit acknowledgement when sample count < threshold.
Inline postmortem suggestions rely on simple text-matching heuristics initially — risk of false positives. Plan: allow users to dismiss suggestions and provide feedback to improve ranking.
Adding simulation increases cognitive load during alert creation. Trade-off: make simulation collapsible with an initial succinct summary and offer an 'advanced view' for power users.
Will need to coordinate latency budgets so wizard remains responsive; if backend sampling is slow, fallback to cached estimates with clear freshness indicator.
notes: Design decision 2026-03-05: Use a percentile band + median line for simulation instead of raw event overlays to keep the visualization legible at multiple zoom levels.
Decision 2026-03-09: Place postmortem suggestions in the final 'Review & Save' step to avoid distraction during threshold tuning.
